We know that the derivative of sine is cosine:

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d x}(\sin{x}) = \cos{x}
$$

Since integration is the reverse of differentiation, we see that the integral of cosine is sine:

$$
\int \cos{x}\,\textrm d x = \sin{x} + C
$$

We can discover two other integrals by considering the derivatives of cosine and tangent:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{sin}x\text{ }\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{cos}x+C \\ \int {sec}^{2}x\text{ }\text{d}x & =\operatorname{tan}x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, by considering the derivatives of secant, cosecant, and cotangent, we arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{sec}x\operatorname{tan}x\text{ }\text{d}x & =\operatorname{sec}x+C \\ \int \operatorname{csc}x\operatorname{cot}x\text{ }\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{csc}x+C \\ \int {csc}^{2}x\text{ }\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{cot}x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

With these six formulas, we can integrate many different trigonometric functions.

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that

$$
\int \sin x \, \textrm dx = -\cos x + C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3sin⁡x\,\text{d}x & =3\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3(-cos⁡x)+C \\  & =-3cos⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that

$$
\int \csc x \cot x \, \textrm dx = - \csc x + C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (-csc⁡xcot⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =-\int (csc⁡xcot⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(-csc⁡x)+C \\  & =csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Calculate the integral $\displaystyle{\int} (2\sec^2 x + \sec x \tan x )\, \textrm{d}x.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that 

$$
\int \sec^2 x \, \textrm dx = \tan x + C
$$

and

$$
\int \sec x \tan x \, \textrm dx = \sec x + C.
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\eqalign{
		\int (2\sec^2 x + \sec x \tan x )\, \textrm{d}x& = 2 \int \sec^2 x \, \textrm{d}x+ \int \sec x \tan x \, \textrm{d}x \
										&=2\tan x + \sec x + C.

}
$$

Recall that 

$$
\int \csc^2 x \, \textrm dx = -\cot x + C
$$

and

$$
\int \csc x \cot x \, \textrm dx = -\csc x + C.
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int csc⁡x(csc⁡x+3cot⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int {csc}^{2}⁡x+3csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x+3\int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-cot⁡x-3csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
